https://www.azernews.az/nation/265489.ht.body: Azerbaijan's ruling party condemns Turkish officials' remarks, warns against interference in domestic affairs 13 October 2026 14:24 (UTC+04:00) Akbar Novruz Read more The New Azerbaijan Party (YAP) has issued a statement criticising remarks made by Turkish presidential adviser Oktay Saral and members of the ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP) concerning Azerbaijan, calling on Turkish political figures to respect the country's sovereignty and refrain from interfering in its internal affairs. According to YAP's press service, certain Turkish media outlets and social media platforms, including resources considered close to the AKP government, have for some time disseminated what the party described as false, biased and defamatory information about Azerbaijan. AzerNEWS presents the full statement: For a long time, the dissemination of untrue, biased, slanderous and defamatory information about Azerbaijan has been observed in a number of Turkish media outlets and social media platforms, including information resources known for their proximity to the AKP government. Considering the partnership relations between the New Azerbaijan Party and the Justice and Development Party, as well as the historical bonds of brotherhood and friendship that unite the peoples of Azerbaijan and Türkiye, we have so far demonstrated restraint in dealing with such cases. Our goal has been to prevent irresponsible behaviour by certain circles from negatively affecting relations between our states and peoples. However, the fact that this information campaign against Azerbaijan has recently become more aggressive, systematic and openly defamatory, especially the involvement of a senior adviser to the President of Türkiye and members of parliament from the ruling Justice and Development Party, makes it necessary for us to express our position openly. First of all, we firmly reject attempts to deliberately distort Azerbaijani-Israeli relations, portray these relations as allegedly exceptional and make political accusations against Azerbaijan. The Republic of Azerbaijan maintains normal interstate relations with Israel based on international law and mutual interests. Azerbaijan's position on the Palestinian issue is consistent, clear and principled. Our country has always supported the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people and provided financial and humanitarian assistance to Palestine. Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas and Prime Minister Mohammad Mustafa have visited Azerbaijan at different times. The activities of the Embassy of the State of Palestine in Azerbaijan are also financially supported by the Azerbaijani state. President Ilham Aliyev has repeatedly stated at the highest international platforms that Azerbaijan supports resolving the Palestinian issue on the basis of international law and relevant UN resolutions, in accordance with the two-state principle, with East Jerusalem as the capital of the State of Palestine. Azerbaijan's position on the events in Gaza is also based on humanitarian values, the protection of civilians and international law. Azerbaijan's relations with the Islamic world are likewise based not on political considerations, but on the principles of mutual respect, equality and solidarity. Our country's contributions to strengthening Islamic solidarity are highly appreciated by Muslim states. The fact that the next Summit of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation is planned to be held in Azerbaijan in 2027 is also an expression of the international trust placed in our country. In this regard, we would like to remind everyone that justice, equality, mutual respect and solidarity occupy an important place among the fundamental principles of Islam. No state in the Islamic world has the right to dictate its will to other Muslim nations, interfere in their internal affairs or consider itself superior to others. Claims of serving the unity of the Muslim world should be demonstrated not through hegemonic tendencies, but through equal cooperation and mutual respect. The Azerbaijani people have historically opposed imperialism, colonialism and neocolonial approaches. This principled position remains unchanged today. It is deeply regrettable that Turkish presidential adviser Oktay Saral and members of parliament from the ruling Justice and Development Party have made populist and irresponsible statements without considering the essence of the issue, Azerbaijan's constitutional structure or the legal foundations of freedom of religious belief in our country. Such statements contradict the spirit of fraternal relations between Azerbaijan and Türkiye and may create artificial tensions in the public sphere. The Azerbaijani people have always respected their national, spiritual and religious values. Freedom of religion is guaranteed by our country's Constitution. The Azerbaijani state treats representatives of all religions equally and considers religious diversity to be a richness of our society. The rules applied in education are based on the principles of equality, secularism, the rule of law and ensuring equal opportunities for all citizens. Under the Constitution of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Azerbaijan is a secular state. This principle is also enshrined in the Constitution of the Republic of Türkiye. Therefore, it is unacceptable for Azerbaijan's secular state structure and education policy to become subjects of political manipulation. In Türkiye itself, political discussions surrounding religious and secular values are deepening polarisation in society. We believe that using sensitive issues such as the headscarf as a means of political manipulation and division serves neither the unity of the Turkish people nor the solidarity of the Muslim world as a whole. Using such issues as a means of political pressure against Azerbaijan is particularly unacceptable. We call on the AKP government to refrain from this harmful policy. The insults, slander and defamatory comments directed against the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, the Victorious Supreme Commander-in-Chief Ilham Aliyev, through various information resources have also caused justified indignation among the Azerbaijani public. The principle of “One nation, two states,” established by National Leader Heydar Aliyev, constitutes the moral and political foundation of Azerbaijan–Türkiye relations. However, the essence of this historic expression must not be distorted. It refers to one nation and two independent states. This principle in no way provides grounds for one state to interfere in the internal affairs of another or impose its political and ideological approaches on the other. The Azerbaijani people have aspired to independence for centuries, restored their statehood and today, under the leadership of President Ilham Aliyev, live in a sovereign state pursuing an independent domestic and foreign policy. The New Azerbaijan Party believes that representatives of the Justice and Development Party, particularly those holding senior state positions, should demonstrate political responsibility in their statements and respect the sovereignty, constitutional structure and internal affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan. We hope that the relevant political circles in Türkiye will draw the appropriate conclusions from such irresponsible statements and refrain from steps that could harm Azerbaijani–Turkish relations. Tags: Foreign Policy New Azerbaijan Party (YAP) Azerbaijan-Turkiye

https://24.kg/en/article/bishkek-needs-5.body: Around 270,000 children attend schools in Bishkek, although the city’s schools are designed to accommodate just 120,000 students. Education Minister Dogdurkul Kendirbaeva made the statement at a meeting of the Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on Constitutional Legislation, State Structure, Local Government and Regulations during discussions on the draft state budget for 2027. According to the minister, the influx of students from other regions is placing additional pressure on the capital’s schools. This year alone, another 12,800 children who are not residents of Bishkek enrolled in the city’s schools. Kendirbaeva said that if the current growth rate continues, another 50–60 schools will need to be built. Under existing standards, each classroom should accommodate 30–35 students. Twenty new schools are currently under construction in Bishkek with state budget funding. Kendirbaeva noted that the capital had never previously had so many schools under construction at the same time. In addition, the Ministry of Education requested funds for school meals during the drafting of the state budget for 2027.

Of these, 668 seats will be allocated to regional maslikhats, 626 to city maslikhats and 2,153 to district maslikhats", Yerman said. Under the decree, the Central Election Commission was instructed to take the necessary measures to organize and conduct early elections to maslikhats. The government and the akims (regional governors and city mayors) of Astana, the regions, Almaty and Shymkent were tasked with providing organizational, logistical and financial support for the elections. On September 24, 2026, Tokayev announced plans to hold early elections to maslikhats at all levels while speaking at the first session of the Kazakhstan People's Council (Qazaqstan Khalyq Kenesi). On August 23, 2026, Kazakhstan held elections to the first convocation of the Kurultai, the country's new unicameral parliament, established under the Constitution that entered into force on July 1, 2026. https://www.trend.az/azerbaijan/politics.body: Home Azerbaijan Politics Azerbaijan parliament ratifies Non-Aligned youth body host deal Politics Document 13 October 2026 12:53 (UTC +04:00) Photo: wikipedia Alish Abdulla Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 13. The Azerbaijani Parliament has ratified the Host Country Agreement regarding the Secretariat of the Non-Aligned Movement Youth Organization (NAMYO), which was submitted for consideration at today’s plenary session of the parliament, Trend ’s correspondent reports from the event. During the session, it was noted that the purpose of the agreement, signed in Baku on September 10, 2026, is to create conditions for the NAMYO Secretariat to effectively perform its functions and duties in Azerbaijan, define its legal status, privileges and immunities, and regulate relations between the Government of Azerbaijan and the organization. The agreement consists of a preamble and 12 articles. The preamble refers to the establishment of the Non-Aligned Movement Youth Network, the creation of the Youth Organization based on the Shusha Declaration adopted in 2022, and the provisions of its Statute, which stipulate that its headquarters be located in Baku. The document establishes the Secretariat’s status as a legal entity, granting it the right to conclude contracts, acquire and dispose of movable and immovable property (excluding land), and initiate legal proceedings. It also defines the inviolability of the Secretariat’s premises, property, archives and documents, as well as the privileges and immunities of its staff members in relation to the performance of their official duties. These privileges and immunities are granted to staff members to enable them to perform their functions and not for their personal benefit. The agreement provides for the Secretariat’s exemption from taxes, customs duties and related charges on goods imported or exported for official use. It also grants the Secretariat the right to hold currency, maintain foreign currency accounts, transfer funds and convert currencies. Certain privileges do not apply to staff members who are citizens of Azerbaijan or permanent residents of the country. The Government of Azerbaijan undertakes to provide the Secretariat with suitable premises, extend the necessary financial support for its operations and ensure appropriate living conditions for its staff members. The annual financial contribution allocated from the state budget is capped at 877,114 manat ($515,950). The Secretariat submits its projected annual budget to the Government, and the allocated financial contribution is transferred to its bank account no later than March 1 of each year. Responsibility for maintaining the premises and covering utility expenses rests with the Secretariat. The document also establishes procedures for issuing visas free of charge to staff members and their family members entering Azerbaijan for official purposes, providing accreditation cards to relevant individuals, and notifying the Government of changes in personnel. The agreement enters into force on the date the organization receives official notification from the Government confirming the completion of internal procedures required for its implementation. Amendments to the agreement may be made through separate protocols upon mutual consent of the parties. Any disputes arising from its interpretation or application will be resolved through negotiations between the parties. The draft law on the approval of the "Host Country Agreement between the Government of Azerbaijan and the Non-Aligned Movement Youth Organization regarding the Secretariat of the Non-Aligned Movement Youth Organization" was adopted in a single reading following discussions. https://www.trend.az/azerbaijan/4233850..body: Home Azerbaijan Chronicles of Victory: President Ilham Aliyev interviewed by Turkish Haber Turk TV channel on October 13, 2020 (PHOTO/VIDEO) Azerbaijan News 13 October 2026 07:00 (UTC +04:00) BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 13. On September 27, 2020, in response to a large-scale provocation of Armenian armed forces along the front line, the Azerbaijani army launched a counter-offensive operation, later named "Iron Fist". The 44-day Second Karabakh War led to the end of almost 30-year occupation and restoration of Azerbaijan's territorial integrity. On 13 October, President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev was interviewed by the Turkish Haber Türk TV channel. On 14 October, the TV channel broadcast the interview with the head of state. Trend presents the interview. - We are with the President of Azerbaijan, Mr. Ilham Aliyev. Mr. President, you have a busy schedule, both at the front and in diplomacy. Thank you very much for your time with Haber Türk. - Thank you. - Mr. President, a meeting between Armenia and Azerbaijan took place in Moscow, which lasted 11 and a half hours. But after that meeting, Armenia bombarded the city of Ganja and targeted civilians with particular cruelty. It is noteworthy here that Armenia aims at Azerbaijan from its own territory. Why did Armenia need this attack at a time when the meeting was held at the diplomatic level? Have you received the desired support from the world community or any messages on this issue? - This dirty policy of Armenia is understandable because they resort to such heinous actions whenever they are defeated on the battlefield. The display of cruelty towards civilians and unarmed population is a common thing for them. The Azerbaijani people saw this in the example of the Khojaly genocide. This time the Azerbaijani Army, having carried out a successful operation along the entire front, liberated several cities and villages. Our operation to liberate us from the occupation continues successfully. This morning, I was informed that the Azerbaijani Army has achieved even more impressive successes in this direction. We will provide this information at the right time. The reason for this treacherous attack by Armenia is that they are trying to expand the geography of this conflict and involve the Collective Security Treaty Organization of which they are a member. This is why they bombard Azerbaijani lands, civilians and provoke us to retaliate. But as I said, our revenge would be on the battlefield. We never take any action against civilians. All our goals are military. From the first days of the operation, military targets were reviewed again, and we eliminated them with precise and aimed fire. The Armenian army suffered a lot of damage. We have destroyed more than 200 tanks, two S-300 anti-aircraft installations, and numerous other pieces of equipment. A total of 33 tanks and other hardware have been taken as trophies. This is another terrorist act on the part of Armenia, but it cannot break the will of the Azerbaijani people. We will fight the enemy with even greater determination, we will liberate our lands with even greater zeal, and we will raise the flag of Azerbaijan in all the occupied lands. As for the reaction of international organizations and the international community to this, as always, Turkey has openly and unequivocally supported us on this issue again. The statements of my dear brother Recep Tayyip Erdogan, the statements of other high-ranking officials were further manifestations of the position of brotherhood. Pakistan and its Prime Minister have made a very positive statement, showing great solidarity. Other countries have made similar statements. But I can't say that it was widespread on a global scale. However, it is as clear as day. A statement is made about a ceasefire, but such a cowardly attack is organized less than a day later. This shows yet again who is not interested in a ceasefire. I said that our goal is to return the citizens of Azerbaijan to all the occupied lands. I said that the ceasefire would allow things to move from a military to political and diplomatic levels. At the diplomatic level, this issue should be resolved around the negotiating table, Armenia should withdraw from the other occupied territories, Azerbaijani citizens should return there and peace should be established. But it seems that Armenia's plans were completely different. They believed that by using this ceasefire, they could reduce their military losses, gain time, mobilize new forces and thus continue their attacks on Azerbaijan. They were wrong. I said that if Armenia did not act positively, they would regret it, and I was right. - Mr. President, your Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov and Armenian Foreign Minister held a meeting that lasted 11 and a half hours. When this meeting was underway, you said that you have one condition – they should provide a timetable, in other words, a timetable for Armenia's withdrawal from Karabakh. Was the timetable provided at the Moscow meeting? Did Moscow submit any project or plan related to the future of Karabakh? - No, the timetable was not provided, but we did not particularly insist on that because we were satisfied with the provisions of the Moscow agreement, the Moscow statement that met our interests. I should also say that the Moscow discussions dragged on because there were plans to include articles that did not suit us in this statement. We didn't know about that. When our foreign minister arrived in Moscow and sat down at the negotiating table, proposals were presented to both ministers. Naturally, I was informed as we were in constant contact. I set out our conditions, outside of which no arrangements were possible. This is why, given the situation, we have slightly softened our position in relation to the timetable. But this does not mean that there will be no timetable. There will be one. When? This will be established during the discussions. It was indicated in the statement that the discussions would be resumed on the basis of the fundamental principles, i.e., the Madrid principles, which confirm the return of our occupied lands to Azerbaijan. At the same time, the format of negotiations remains unchanged. In particular, negotiations will be held between Armenia and Azerbaijan. The participation of any representative of the so-called "Nagorno-Karabakh republic" in these talks is not negotiable. We are satisfied with that. Our expectation was that negotiations should start immediately and the timetable should be presented to us within these negotiations. We must be satisfied with this timetable. In other words, it cannot be a long process. We have waited for 30 years. The patience of the Azerbaijani people has already run out. I am sure that if negotiations resume, this timetable will be provided to us. However, the violation of this agreement, of this statement on the part of Armenia shows that they simply intend to gain time and continue attacks on Azerbaijan. - Mr. President, Armenia is making attempts related to the independence of Nagorno-Karabakh. Armenia is trying to solicit political pressure from France, Russia and other countries with a strong Armenian diaspora. You are taking a decisive position on the issue of liberating Karabakh from occupation. What is your model related to Karabakh after its liberation? Will it be an autonomous region or an independent entity? What will be the process related to Karabakh like? - First of all, I have to say that the attempts currently being made by Armenia are inappropriate and very harmful for themselves because no country will ever grant independence to Nagorno-Karabakh, which is an integral part of Azerbaijan and belongs to it from the point of view of international law. No country will recognize it. This being the case, all such attempts will be fruitless. The territorial integrity of Azerbaijan is recognized by the whole world. https://www.trend.az/casia/turkmenistan/.body: Home Central Asia Turkmenistan Malaysia’s economy minister to lead 20+ companies to Turkmenistan’s OGT (Exclusive) Turkmenistan Interview 13 October 2026 08:00 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Malaysian Ministry of Economy /Instagram Fuad Namazov Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 13. Malaysia’s Economy Minister will lead a delegation of more than 20 companies to Turkmenistan’s OGT 2026. Turkmen Energy Forum provided the information to Trend in an exclusive comment ahead of the International Conference and Exhibition "Oil and Gas of Turkmenistan" (OGT 2026). "Malaysia’s Minister of Economy, Tuan Haji Akmal Nasrullah bin Mohd Nasir, will lead a high-level government and business delegation to Turkmenistan for OGT 2026, bringing representatives of more than 20 Malaysian companies to Ashgabat on 21–23 October," Turkmen Energy Forum said. According to the organization, the visit is set to bring a large Malaysian government and business delegation to Ashgabat. "The visit will mark Malaysia’s largest coordinated presence at the International Conference and Exhibition "Oil and Gas of Turkmenistan", including the country’s first dedicated Malaysia Pavilion at OGT," the forum noted. The organization added that the Malaysian delegation will include 14 companies from the oil and gas services and equipment sector, participating through an MPRC market-access initiative. "Fourteen Malaysian oil and gas services and equipment (OGSE) companies will participate through an international market-access initiative of Malaysia Petroleum Resources Corporation (MPRC), aimed at developing business links and long-term partnerships in Turkmenistan," the Turkmen Energy Forum said. Notably, diplomatic relations between Turkmenistan and Malaysia were established in 1992, with embassies subsequently opened in Ashgabat and Kuala Lumpur, reflecting a steady institutionalization of bilateral ties over time. The core pillar of economic cooperation is the energy sector, where Malaysia’s state oil and gas company PETRONAS has operated in Turkmenistan since 1996 under production-sharing agreements in the Caspian Sea offshore blocks. The partnership entered a new stage during Malaysian Prime Minister Dato’ Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s visit to Turkmenistan in June 2026. New agreements included a Production Sharing Agreement covering offshore Blocks 19 and 20 in the Turkmen sector of the Caspian Sea, as well as cooperation on 2D seismic studies covering Blocks 11, 12, 13 and 14. https://www.trend.az/azerbaijan/politics.body: Home Azerbaijan Politics Azerbaijan’s parliament ratifies Climate Week deal with UN climate body Politics Document 13 October 2026 11:54 (UTC +04:00) Photo: National Assembly of the Republic of Azerbaijan Alish Abdulla Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 13. The Azerbaijani Parliament has ratified the memorandum of understanding signed between Azerbaijan and the UNFCCC, submitted for discussion at a plenary session of the parliament today, Trend ’s correspondent reports from the event. During the session, it was noted that the memorandum was signed in Bonn on September 1, 2026, and in Baku on September 2. The document outlines the organizational, financial, and legal aspects regarding the hosting of Climate Week 4 and the 30th meeting of the Adaptation Committee in Azerbaijan, as well as the obligations of the Government of Azerbaijan and the UN Secretariat. Climate Week is an international event that brings together representatives from states, international organizations, the private sector, and other stakeholders to accelerate the implementation of climate-related decisions adopted under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, to exchange experiences, and to discuss practical solutions. Climate Week 4 was held in Baku from September 7 to 11, 2026. The Adaptation Committee is a body operating under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change that addresses issues related to adaptation to the adverse effects of climate change. The committee works to provide technical support and recommendations to the Parties, promote the exchange of information and best practices, and strengthen cooperation among relevant institutions. The 30th meeting of the Committee was held in Baku from September 14 to 17, 2026. According to the memorandum, the Government of Azerbaijan is responsible for providing the venue, logistics, technical infrastructure, security and protocol arrangements, and other necessary organizational elements for Climate Week 4, as well as covering the relevant costs stipulated in the memorandum. Logistics and other organizational expenses for the 30th meeting of the Adaptation Committee are covered by the Secretariat. The annexes to the memorandum of understanding specify the buildings, meeting venues and facilities, equipment, supplies and utilities, host country support staff, and catering services required for holding Climate Week 4. The Secretariat is responsible for preparing and managing the event program, inviting participants and experts, providing them with necessary organizational information, and arranging relevant payments for participants funded by the Secretariat. The document also establishes provisions regarding tax and customs exemptions, visa matters, privileges and immunities, the inviolability of event venues, personal data protection, and the liabilities of the parties. Following discussions, the draft law on the approval of the "Memorandum of understanding between the Government of Azerbaijan and the Secretariat of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the Kyoto Protocol, and the Paris Agreement regarding Climate Week 4 and the 30th meeting of the Adaptation Committee" was put to a vote and adopted in a single reading.
